name: Span
doc: Source span for error reporting.

name: Comment
doc: A source comment (`;;`, `#`, or `#= … =#`), captured by the lexer as trivia so the formatter can re-emit it. `line` is the 1-based source line; `text` is the verbatim comment text starting at its marker (leading indentation is dropped — the formatter re-indents).

name: Program
doc: Top-level program. One `.lolo` file is one `Program`.

fields.name: app
fields.doc: `app NAME [vVERSION]` line.

fields.name: type_aliases
fields.doc: Top-level type aliases (scoped to the whole file).

fields.name: uses
fields.doc: File-scoped `uses Alias from "path"` declarations — legal ABOVE any `orbital` block (orbital-import Stage A). Lowering merges these into every orbital's own `uses` (local alias wins on collision), which is what lets a top-level `orbital X = Alias.orbitals.Y` reference resolve `Alias` through the same per-orbital `ctx` loop the compiler already runs — no change needed there. Distinct from `Orbital.uses`, which stays legal too (per-orbital, unchanged).

fields.name: orbitals
fields.doc: Orbital declarations.

fields.name: comments
fields.doc: Source comments (trivia), in source order. Re-emitted by the formatter, interleaved by source line; ignored by lowering.

name: AppHeader
doc: `app NAME "VERSION" [ modifiers ]` header.

fields.name: theme
fields.doc: `theme "<key>"` on the line after the header — the APP-level skin every orbital's `@currentTheme` seeds from unless the orbital declares its own `theme`. A full `<base>-<light|dark>` registry key, or an inline `theme { … }` token definition.

fields.name: themes
fields.doc: `themes: ["<key>", …]` — the registry themes the program switches to inside a page.

fields.name: locales
fields.doc: `locales [en, ar, sl]` — the locales this program ships.

fields.name: store
fields.doc: `store: Driver` — the default store-driver orbital for persistent entities that name none.

fields.name: egress
fields.doc: `egress: ["https://host", …]` — the origins `http` may reach.

fields.name: inbound
fields.doc: `inbound: ["name", …]` — the hook names (`/api/hooks/<name>`) the program accepts.

fields.name: os_grants
fields.doc: `fs:` / `exec:` / `net:` / `env:` / `stdio:` / `sys:` / `desktop:` — the `os/` grants of every orbital.

fields.name: deployment
fields.doc: `deployment: { unit: [Orbital, …] }`, units in source order.

fields.name: public
fields.doc: `public: "./public"` — a folder copied verbatim to the built site's root.

fields.name: site
fields.doc: `origin:` / `icon:` / `siteName:` / `signIn:` site modifiers.

fields.name: legacy_lines
fields.doc: The modifiers were written as loose lines after `app` (the pre-bracket form) — still parsed, reported as `ORB_L_APP_HEADER_LEGACY`.

fields.name: config
fields.doc: App-level `config { ... }` block, declared right after the header (orbital-import Stage A, `OrbitalSchema.config`) — ORGANISM-wide knobs every orbital's traits may forward with `@config.<knob>`.

name: ThemeDecl
doc: A `theme` declaration — either a registry-key reference (`theme "<key>"`, lowers to `ThemeRef::Reference`) or an inline token definition (`theme { name: "…" tokens { … } variants { … } }`, lowers to `ThemeRef::Inline`).

name: InlineTheme
doc: Inline theme definition — the `.lolo` surface of `ThemeDefinition`.

name: ThemeTokenMaps
doc: The theme token categories; entries keep source order. The five legacy maps (`colors`/`radii`/`spacing`/`typography`/`shadows`) are free-form; the typed axes `typeScale`/`geometry`/`elevation`/`surface` take only their flat string fields (camelCase keys, see [`THEME_TYPED_AXIS_KEYS`]). Nested typed fields (type scale/intents) and density/motion/iconography stay `.orb`-JSON-only.

name: TypeAlias
doc: `type Name [T] = ...` declaration. The optional `type_param` is the single entity-type variable used in parameterized shapes (`type Browsable T = ...`); it's bound when the alias is applied via `::` annotation.

fields.name: type_param
fields.doc: Single-ident type parameter — either the bare form (`T` in `type Browsable T = ...`) or the name half of the parenthesized kinded form (`E` in `type Foo (E : Entity) = ...`). `None` for non-parameterized aliases.

fields.name: type_param_kind
fields.doc: The kind half of a parenthesized kinded type parameter (`Entity` in `type Foo (E : Entity) = ...`) — one of `Type | Entity | Trait | Page | Orbital | Event`. `None` for the bare form or when there's no parameter at all. Only `Entity` is acted on by the compiler today (increment 3-I: `(E : Entity)` on an `Event` alias monomorphizes to the using trait's bound entity); other kinds are stored but inert.

name: TypeBody
doc: Body of a type alias. In addition to the legacy sum/struct/alias forms, aliases can name composable shapes: `Entity`, `Trait`, `Page`, `Orbital`. Composition via `&` merges two bodies of the same kind.

fields.name: Enum
fields.doc: `type Status = a | b | c` enum form.

fields.name: Struct
fields.doc: `type Coord = { lat: float, lng: float! }` struct form. Each entry is `(field_name, type, required)` — `required` mirrors the optional `!` marker after the field's type (`name : T` → false, `name : T!` → true). Carrying it through the AST instead of dropping it (per the old `Vec<(String, TypeExpr)>` shape) is what lets the codegen emit lolo struct fields as optional-by-default in TS, matching lolo's authoring semantics.

fields.name: Alias
fields.doc: `type Money = number` nominal alias form.

fields.name: Entity
fields.doc: `type Patient = Entity [persistent: patients] { id : string! ... }`.

fields.name: Trait
fields.doc: `type Browsable T = Trait Browse.traits.BrowseItemBrowse -> T`. `linked_entity_param` is the name of the type parameter that binds to the trait's linkedEntity slot (e.g. `T`). Nominal references to named entities can instead be expressed via `TypeExpr::Named` in `linked_entity`.

fields.name: Page
fields.doc: `type ListPage T = Page -> Trait[Browsable T]`.

fields.name: Orbital
fields.doc: `type CrudOrbital T = Orbital { entity: T; traits: ...; page: ... }`.

fields.name: Event
fields.doc: `type BrowseItemLoaded = Event BrowseItem` or `type OrderShipped = Event OrderShipment [external]` or `type Err = Event { message: string }` or `type XLoaded = Event X "Fired when X finishes loading"`. The payload type can be any TypeExpr: a named entity / type alias, an anonymous struct body, or a primitive. The optional bracket modifier sets the event's cross-orbital scope; unmarked defaults to `internal`. The optional trailing string literal sets the event description; it flows through to `EmitDefinition.description` on every emit reference. Lowers to one `EmitDefinition { event, scope, description, payload }` per reference in a trait's `emits: [...]` list.

fields.name: Composition
fields.doc: `A & B & C` composition. Resolver flattens, checks kind compatibility, merges fields / traits / pages depending on the kind of the members.

name: EventScopeAst
doc: Event scope marker parsed from `[internal]` / `[external]` after an `Event ...` type body. `None` in the outer `Option<EventScopeAst>` means the author did not annotate; the lowerer defaults to Internal.

name: TypeKind
doc: Kind tag used by the type resolver for composition-compatibility checks. Not parsed from source — derived from the `TypeBody` variant.

name: TypeAnnotation
doc: `Name :: TypeName [Arg1 Arg2 ...]` annotation above a declaration.  Applied to entity / trait / page / orbital blocks. The parser attaches this to the corresponding AST node; the type resolver checks the body against the named type (with `type_args` substituted for the alias's type parameters).

fields.name: type_name
fields.doc: Dotted name of the type alias to apply (e.g. `"Auditable"` or `"Lib.CrudOrbital"` once cross-file resolution is wired).

fields.name: type_args
fields.doc: Positional type arguments. Each is a single identifier that resolves to another type alias or entity name.

name: Orbital
doc: `orbital Name [:: TypeAnnotation] { ... }` declaration.

fields.name: type_annotation
fields.doc: Optional `::` type annotation above the orbital declaration.

fields.name: expects
fields.doc: `expects ...` declarations — consumer-side requirements on sibling orbitals (docs/Almadar_LOLO_Expects_Proposal.md §3).

fields.name: extra_entities
fields.doc: Entity declarations beyond the first. The first `entity` block is the orbital's primary entity; later blocks lower into the IR's `auxiliary_entities` (previously the parser silently last-wins REPLACED the primary — C-VALIDATE-MULTI-ENTITY-ORBITAL).

fields.name: theme
fields.doc: `theme "<name>"` / `theme { … }` — the orbital's active skin: a reference to a theme in the built-in `@almadar-ui/themes/` registry, or an inline token definition carried by the orbital itself. `@currentTheme` resolves to this at render time. `None` ⇒ no skin declared (the host omits `data-theme`, or the assembler sets it via the factory `theme` param).

fields.name: body
fields.doc: Free-floating s-expression body items at the orbital level (e.g., `(behavior/compose { ... })`). Lowered to top-level effects on the orbital that the Compose pass will resolve.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: `orbital Name = Alias.orbitals.Y { ... }` — the dotted reference path (`"Alias.orbitals.Y"`) when this orbital is a REFERENCE to an imported orbital, not an inline definition (orbital-import Stage A, mirrors `Page.reference`/`Trait.reference`). `entity`/`extra_entities`/ `pages` MUST be empty when this is `Some` — the upstream organism owns them; the fields below are the override surface. `traits` (Stage B) holds SIBLING trait declarations authored in the reference body — the upstream's own traits arrive at inline, never here.

fields.name: entity_rebind
fields.doc: `entity NAME` override body — rebinds the imported orbital's primary entity, exactly as `-> Entity` does on a trait reference.

fields.name: entity_rebind_tags
fields.doc: The entity-header bracket after `entity [Name]` in an import body (`[persistent: tbl]`, `[runtime]`, `[local]`, flags), overriding the materialized primary entity's persistence/collection/flags.

fields.name: fields_remap
fields.doc: `fields { up: local }` — primary-entity field renames the imported traits read/write, lifted from the trait form's `fields {}` to orbital scope. Third tuple element is the KEY token's span (Stage C `.lolo` spans), for `ORB_O_*` diagnostics that name this key.

fields.name: pages_remap
fields.doc: `pages { "/up": "/local" }` — route-path remap. An unmapped upstream path keeps its own value; required whenever two imports of the same orbital would otherwise collide on route. Third element: KEY span.

fields.name: page_modifiers
fields.doc: `pages { "/up": "/local" [access: …] }` — page modifiers per remap entry, keyed by the UPSTREAM path, in source order.

fields.name: omit
fields.doc: `omit { A B }` — trait/aux-entity names to drop from the imported set. Omitting a trait some other imported trait embeds is an error, not a silent drop (checked post-inline). Second element: the name token's span.

fields.name: only
fields.doc: `only { A B }` — trait/aux-entity names to KEEP; everything else is dropped. Mutually exclusive with `omit` in authoring practice, not enforced by the grammar.

fields.name: config_overrides
fields.doc: `config { ... }` override body — overrides the referenced orbital's OWN declared knobs (`Orbital.config`) 1:1; a dotted `Trait.knob` is the upstream (pre-prefix) escape hatch.

fields.name: events_remap
fields.doc: `events { UP: LOCAL }` — orbital-scope event rename, applied to every trait in the imported set (emits AND listen keys), same rule as the trait reference form's `events {}`.

fields.name: roles_remap
fields.doc: `roles { approver: [owner, project_manager]  employee: team_member }` (Stage B) — upstream role vocabulary word → one or more consumer roster role names. Order preserved for the formatter. Third element: the KEY (upstream word) token's span.

fields.name: entities_remap
fields.doc: `entities { Employee: Person }` (Stage B) — out-of-orbital upstream entity name → consumer entity name. Identity (`X: X`) is legal. Third element: the KEY token's span.

fields.name: mounts
fields.doc: `pages { "/up": "/local" -> TraitA, TraitB }` mount tails (Stage B), keyed by the UPSTREAM path — sibling trait names (declared in `traits` below) to mount on that page in addition to its own. Third element: the upstream path key's span (same span `pages_remap` records for the same path).

fields.name: config
fields.doc: `config { ... }` — an INLINE orbital's own declared knobs (orbital-import Stage A, `Orbital.config`). Empty for a reference-form orbital, whose declared knobs live upstream; always empty together with `config_overrides`, which is the reference form's override surface for THIS field on the orbital it references.

fields.name: extend_fields
fields.doc: `extend { <field-decl>+ }` (Stage C) — full entity-field declarations appended to the primary entity, AFTER `fields {}` renames apply. Unlike `fields {}` (rename-only), each entry is a whole new field.

fields.name: mock_overrides
fields.doc: `mock { field: "a, b" }` — the import's own sample data for fields of the materialized primary entity, replacing the upstream `@mock`.

fields.name: retype_fields
fields.doc: `retype { name : type = default }` — replaces the type/default of fields the upstream primary entity already declares (after `fields {}` renames).

fields.name: trait_overrides
fields.doc: `traits { UpstreamTrait [-> Entity] { events fields config listens emitsScope } }` — per-imported-trait overrides, keyed by the UPSTREAM trait name.

fields.name: import_listens
fields.doc: Orbital-import `listens { Source.EVENT -> Target.TRIGGER }` — routes into the imported set; each carries its `target_trait`.

fields.name: alias_entity_refs
fields.doc: Entity names a spec shape reaches through a `uses` alias (`owner : Inner.Customer` names `Customer`). Set by the projection pass; they are legal relation targets, supplied by the imported spec.

fields.name: os_grants
fields.doc: `orbital Name [ fs: …, exec: … ]` — this orbital's own `os/` grants.

name: EntityRebindTags
doc: Entity-header tags written on an import body's `entity` line.

name: TraitOverride
doc: One `traits { UpstreamTrait [-> Entity] { ... } }` entry of an orbital-import body.

fields.name: trait_name
fields.doc: The trait's UPSTREAM name.

name: UseDecl
doc: `uses Alias from "path"`.

fields.name: lazy
fields.doc: `uses lazy A from "…"` — compiled to its own `.orb`, loaded when one of its pages is opened.

fields.name: config
fields.doc: Optional `{ config { ... } }` body (orbital-import Stage A) — overrides the imported behavior's ORGANISM-wide `config {}` knobs for every orbital taken from this alias. Empty for the bare form.

name: ExpectedAccess
doc: The `@read|@create|@update|@delete` directives of an entity body or an `expects entity` shape.

fields.name: access_waivers
fields.doc: `@<op> none "<reason>"` waivers, as `(op, reason)`.

name: ExpectsDecl
doc: One `expects ...` declaration inside an orbital block.

name: ExpectsKind
doc: The three expectation forms. `shape` reuses the entity field-declaration grammar verbatim — it is the consumer's declared minimal contract.

fields.name: Identity
fields.doc: `expects entity [Name] [identity] [{ fields }]` — bare (neither name nor shape) is the hand-authoring escape hatch.

fields.name: Entity
fields.type: String, Option<Vec<EntityField>>, Option<Persistence>, bool, bool, ExpectedAccess, Vec<SExpression>
fields.doc: `expects entity Name [persistent, shared] [{ fields, @read … }]` — shape omitted = opaque reference.

fields.name: Event
fields.doc: `expects trait Trait { emits { EVENT } }` — one per emitted event; names pass through verbatim.

fields.name: Page
fields.doc: `expects page "/articles/:slug"` — a route a sibling orbital declares and this one navigates to. The provider's PATTERN, which a navigate effect's static prefix cannot supply.

fields.name: State
fields.doc: `expects trait T { state paid }` — the provider trait declares this state; `state paid @holds <expr>` adds a proposition over `@entity` that holds while the trait is in it.

fields.name: Transition
fields.doc: `expects trait T { state idle { PAY -> paid } }` — the provider trait has this transition; `@ensures <expr>` lines after the target add its outcome contract.

fields.name: Config
fields.doc: `expects config { stdio : string = "pipe" }` — one per knob: a trait of the program declares it, of this type and, when stated, with this default.

name: Entity
doc: `entity Name [:: TypeAnnotation] [persistence] { fields... }`.

fields.name: type_annotation
fields.doc: Optional `::` type annotation above the entity declaration.

fields.name: shared
fields.doc: `shared` header tag — orthogonal to persistence: entity state shared across all bound traits vs copied per-trait.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: `identity` header tag — orthogonal to both persistence and `shared`: this entity types the ambient `@user` viewer. An app-owned user directory is both persisted and the identity, so it cannot be a persistence mode.

fields.name: local
fields.doc: `local` header tag — `[persistent: x, local]`: the rows live in the browser.

fields.name: seed_mock
fields.doc: `mock` header tag — seed an empty browser store from the shared mock seeder.

fields.name: store
fields.doc: `store: Driver` header tag — the store-driver orbital answering this entity's row asks.

fields.name: instances
fields.doc: `instances [ { … }, … ]` — written-out rows the entity starts with.

fields.name: locale_instances
fields.doc: `instances <lang> [ … ]` — the written-out rows for one declared locale.

fields.name: read_policy
fields.doc: `@read <sexpr>` — a per-row predicate evaluated with `@entity` bound to the candidate row and `@user` to the viewer. ANDed with any call-site `filter:`; enforced once, for every trait that fetches this entity — the read-access twin of `@create`/`@update`/`@delete` below.

fields.name: create_policy
fields.doc: `@create <sexpr>` — evaluated with `@entity` bound to the INCOMING data about to become a row (no row exists yet) and `@user` to the viewer.

fields.name: update_policy
fields.doc: `@update <sexpr>` — evaluated with `@entity` bound to the EXISTING row before mutation (fetched fresh) and `@user` to the viewer.

fields.name: delete_policy
fields.doc: `@delete <sexpr>` — same binding shape as `@update`.

fields.name: access_waivers
fields.doc: `@<op> none "<reason>"` — a DECLARED omission, keyed by op name (`read`/`create`/`update`/`delete`) with the author's stated reason. Behaves exactly like leaving the directive out; it exists so a lint can tell a considered omission from a forgotten one.

fields.name: invariants
fields.doc: `@invariant <expr>` lines: propositions every stored row satisfies, proved by `orb validate`.

name: Persistence
doc: Persistence tag.

name: EntityField
doc: One field on an entity.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: `!` modifier on the type.

fields.name: nullable
fields.doc: `?` modifier on the type.

fields.name: is_key
fields.doc: Trailing `@key` annotation.

fields.name: is_unique
fields.doc: Trailing `@unique` annotation.

fields.name: is_intrinsic
fields.doc: Trailing `@intrinsic` annotation. Marks the field as machinery/view-state the owning trait computes internally; it travels WITH the trait on a `linkedEntity` rebind and is NOT required to pre-exist on the target.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Trailing `@description "..."` annotation — human/semantic description of the field. Authoring/build-time metadata (factory-signature catalog, embeddings, curation remap); the runtime ignores it.

fields.name: synonyms
fields.doc: Trailing `@synonyms "..."` annotation — user-vocabulary synonyms (free text) feeding catalog search / curation field-matching.

fields.name: mock
fields.doc: Trailing `@mock "..."` annotation — a declared literal value (or comma-separated candidate list) the seeder uses AS-IS, never through a domain-name lookup table. Authoring metadata only, like `description`/ `synonyms` — the runtime ignores it.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Default value `= sexpr`.

fields.name: derived
fields.doc: `derived` field flag with the derivation expression.

name: PayloadOfTarget
doc: What a `@payload <arg>` dependent type resolves against — the two spellings `TypeExpr::EventPayloadOf` carries. Kept as one enum (not a string convention) so every consumer switches on a closed shape instead of re-parsing a leading sigil out of a string.

fields.name: ConfigKnob
fields.doc: `@payload @config.<knob>` — the payload of the event that config knob names. Resolved post-inline (L2), against the call site's folded config default — see `orbital-compiler::phases::inline::sigil_types`.

fields.name: SiblingMember
fields.doc: `@payload <member>` — the payload of the event that a SIBLING member of the SAME struct body names. `member` must be declared alongside this field (same `type X = { ... }` / inline object body) and typed `event`. Resolved at L1, against literal struct instances authored in the same file — see `types::check_payload_sibling_refs`.

name: TypeExpr
doc: Type expression in field declarations.

fields.name: Primitive
fields.doc: Primitive type (`string`, `int`, `bool`, ...).

fields.name: Named
fields.doc: User-defined named type (e.g. `Status`, `Order`).

fields.name: StringLiteral
fields.doc: String-literal singleton type (`"active"`). Only meaningful inside a `Union` that spells out a finite set of strings — the lowerer detects such unions and emits them as `"type": "string"` + `"values": [...]` on the field, matching the committed `.orb` shape.

fields.name: Array
fields.doc: `[T]` array type.

fields.name: Tuple
fields.doc: `[T1, T2, …]` — a fixed-length tuple (two or more slots).

fields.name: Map
fields.doc: `Map K V` dynamic-key map type — a uniform-value dictionary with arbitrary keys (e.g. `Map string SimulationParameter`). Reserved built-in binary constructor applied by juxtaposition, mirroring Haskell's `Map k v`. Lowers to `Record<K, V>` in codegen. Distinct from the fixed-key `Object` struct: keys aren't known at author time.

fields.name: Object
fields.doc: `{ k: T, ... }` / `{ k: T! }` inline object type. Each entry is `(field_name, type, required)`; the optional `!` marker tracks whether the field is required so the lowerer can emit the matching `required` flag on the resulting `FieldDefinition`.

fields.name: Union
fields.doc: `T | U` union (lowering inlines this to enum values when all members are bare names or string literals).

fields.name: BoundEntityRow
fields.doc: `@entity` — the bound entity's ROW type (self-reference). The sigil already means "the bound entity" throughout the expression grammar; in a payload type position it names that entity's row shape, resolved at compose time against the trait's final `linkedEntity` (monomorphized exactly like an Entity-kinded type parameter's default). Only legal in event payload positions (Event alias bodies, emits/listens payloads).

fields.name: EventPayloadOf
fields.doc: `@payload <knob>` — the declared payload type of the event that the named config knob resolves to. A sigil type constructor applied by JUXTAPOSITION, like `Map K V`; the language has exactly two application forms (Lisp `(fn args)` in expressions, juxtaposition in types) and a third would be an inconsistency.  The argument is a value REFERENCE, not a type — this is the language's first dependent type, so it is deliberately fenced: the knob must be declared on the same trait, resolution is compile-time and total (resolve or hard error), and there is no nesting.  Distinct from the expression-position `@payload.x`, which reads the CURRENT event's payload. Same word, different grammar position, different referent — the parser change is scoped to `parse_type_atom` so the two can never overlap.

fields.name: NamedEntityRow
fields.doc: `@entity <knob>` — the row type of the entity that the named config knob resolves to. The unary sibling of `BoundEntityRow`: same sigil, arity distinguishes "the bound entity" from "the entity that knob names".

fields.name: ExpectedIdentityRow
fields.doc: `@user` — the row type of the identity this orbital `expects`. The identity axis's counterpart to `BoundEntityRow`: lets a reusable atom say "the acting user" without naming whose identity entity that is.

fields.name: Optional
fields.doc: `T?` nullable.

fields.name: FieldOf
fields.doc: `T.f` — the declared type of field `f` of the entity or struct type `T`, legal in every type position. `resolved` is `f`'s own type expression, filled by `lower::projection` before lowering; [`TypeExpr::peel`] reads through it, and field builders record the provenance (`projectedFrom`).

fields.name: RelationMany
fields.doc: `T*` one-to-many relation.

fields.name: RelationManyNonEmpty
fields.doc: `T+` one-or-more relation.

fields.name: Trait
fields.doc: `trait` — value is a `@trait.X` reference. Substituted to embedded trait UI at render time. Allowed only in `config { ... }` blocks.

fields.name: Orbital
fields.doc: `orbital` — an orbital value held as data (`<spec>.orbitals.<O>` plus a recorded §8b import body), or `none`. Never rendered.

fields.name: Behavior
fields.doc: `behavior` — a whole behavior held as data (`behavior/ref`), or `none`. Embedded in a render tree, it runs the program in place.

fields.name: EntityRef
fields.doc: `entity` — value is an entity NAME reference (V4-W5). The stamp records the referenced entity's id on the config field so a declaration-only rename resolves the value by id. Allowed only in `config { ... }` blocks.

fields.name: EventRef
fields.doc: `event` — value is an event NAME reference (V4-W5), id-carried by the stamp like `EntityRef`. Allowed only in `config { ... }` blocks.

fields.name: EventAddress
fields.doc: `EventAddress` — a value addressing a declared external input (`Trait.EVENT`, `Orbital.Trait.EVENT`). Allowed only in `config { ... }` blocks.

fields.name: Slot
fields.doc: `slot` — value is a UI slot name. Validated against `VALID_SLOTS`.

fields.name: Pattern
fields.doc: `pattern` — value is a pattern type name. Validated against `PATTERN_TYPES`.

fields.name: Secret
fields.doc: `secret` — value is a credential REFERENCE (an env-var key name for `resolveCredentialRef`), never secret material itself. Config-only (core's `SECRET_CONFIG_TYPES` contract, I-29): UI renders the knob as a password input; traces/bakes mask it as defense-in-depth.

fields.name: SExpr
fields.doc: `SExpr` — value is a compiled s-expression (the `SExpr` brand from `@almadar/core`). Used for config fields that hold an s-expression (e.g. a `conditionalFields` visibility condition). Emits the recursive `SExpr` TypeScript type (inlined as a local alias in codegen, like `TraitFieldRef`). Allowed only in `config { ... }` blocks.

fields.name: Match
fields.doc: `match @config.<knob> { <pattern> -> <type> ... }` — a compile-time conditional TYPE selected by a config knob's resolved literal (§25). Replaces `@typeWhen` outright: one concept, one spelling. The `_` arm is mandatory and must be last; it lowers to the field's base `field_type`, and every other arm lowers to one entry of the unchanged `PayloadTypeWhen` wire list (`lower_match_field_type`). Legal only as an event-payload field's WHOLE type (`emits`/local `listens`); forbidden everywhere else in the type grammar (entity fields, `expects`, config fields, type-alias/Event-alias bodies, nested inside another type) — see `check_match_types` + `type_expr_config_only_type`/`type_expr_contains_match`.

name: MatchArm
doc: One arm of a type-level `match` (`TypeExpr::Match`). `ty` is restricted to `Primitive`/`[Primitive]` in v1 — anything else is `ELOLO_MATCH_ARM_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` (`check_match_types`).

name: MatchPattern
doc: A type-level match arm's pattern. Compared against a resolved config literal's canonical spelling (`orbital_core::schema::config_literal_spelling`) via `spelling()` below — `Str`/`Word` are interchangeable spellings of the same literal (`"number"` and `number` both spell `"number"`).

name: TraitTypeParam
doc: One trait-level type parameter (Increment 3-II): `(V : Type)` in `trait LookupRun (V : Type, R : Type) -> KeyLookup [lifecycle, instance] { ... }`. Parsed immediately after the trait name, before `::`/`->`/`=`. `kind` is validated against the same six kind names Increment 3-I's alias params accept (`Type | Entity | Trait | Page | Orbital | Event`); only `Type` and `Entity` are meaningfully acted on downstream. A param name is usable in this trait's own `emits`/`listens`/config type positions, lowering each reference to a `"$<name>"` sentinel (3-I's substitution machinery).

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Gap C: optional `= <ident>` declaration default — a primitive name, an entity name, or a struct-alias name, all resolved in the atom's own file.

name: TraitScope
doc: `trait Name [:: TypeAnnotation] -> Entity [category] { ... }` or `trait Name [:: TypeAnnotation] = Alias.traits.Upstream -> Entity { ... }` (reference form). Instance vs collection scope, parsed from the trait modifier list (`[interaction, instance]` / `[interaction, collection]`). Optional in this phase; unmarked traits pass. The type-checker will require one of these in a later phase (see Almadar_Entity_V2_Plan.md Phase 4).

name: Trait
doc: A `trait` declaration: an inline state machine bound to an entity, or a reference to an imported trait with call-site overrides.

fields.name: type_params
fields.doc: Increment 3-II: trait-level type parameters declared `(V : Type, ...)` immediately after the name. Empty for traits that declare none — which is every trait predating this increment, and always empty on a reference-form trait (a reference supplies ARGUMENTS via `::`, not a parameter declaration).

fields.name: type_annotation
fields.doc: Optional `::` type annotation above the trait declaration.

fields.name: linked_entity_span
fields.doc: Where the entity name after `->` is written.

fields.name: entity_rebindable
fields.doc: Set when the binding was authored as `-> @rebindable Entity`. Opts the trait into consumer entity-rebinding via `linkedEntity`. Only meaningful on inline trait definitions (atoms); a reference's `->` IS the rebind, so this is always false there.

fields.name: entity_binding_description
fields.doc: `@description "..."` annotation on the rebindable binding (body-level). Surfaced to the catalog/knob-embeddings so the LLM can discover the binding from intent vocabulary. Only emitted when `entity_rebindable`.

fields.name: entity_binding_synonyms
fields.doc: `@synonyms "..."` annotation on the rebindable binding (body-level).

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: Instance or collection scope marker parsed from the modifier list. `None` today means the trait opted out / predates the modifier. Phase 4 of the V2 migration turns `None` into a warning.

fields.name: local
fields.doc: `local` marker parsed from the same trait-header bracket list. Declares client-only dispatch (see `docs/Almadar_LOLO.md` §7). Undeclared (`false`) is server-gated dispatch — never inferred.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: Author-supplied capability tags parsed from the trait header's bracket list. Anything beyond the scope marker (`instance`/`collection`) and the first category identifier collects here. Free-form strings — the parser doesn't validate against a known set. Source for `OirTrait.capabilities` and downstream `FactorySignature` matching. See `docs/Almadar_Domain_Language.md` Phase 3.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: When `Some`, this trait is a reference to an imported trait, not an inline definition. The reference data carries the dotted path (`Alias.traits.X`) plus per-event override maps. `states`, `initial_state`, `ticks`, and `config` MUST be empty when this is set; the upstream atom owns state-machine topology. `linked_entity`, `listens`, and `emits` may still be set: they translate into the reference's `linkedEntity`, `listens`, and (via `emits_scope`) `emitsScope` overrides.

fields.name: is_inline_synthetic
fields.doc: When `true`, this trait declaration was synthesized by the parser from an inline `@(...)` reference. The formatter uses this marker to reconstruct the original sugar instead of emitting a top-level `trait` declaration.

name: TraitRefBody
doc: Parsed body of a trait-reference call site — the `{ events {} fields {} config {} listens {} emitsScope {} }` shared between the `trait Name = Alias.traits.X { … }` declaration form and the inline `@(Alias.traits.X { … })` sugar. Produced by `Parser::parse_trait_ref_body`.

fields.name: name_override
fields.doc: `name: "InstanceName"` — instance-name override for the reference.

name: TraitRefData
doc: Override payload for a `trait Name = Alias.traits.Upstream { ... }` form.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: Dotted path: e.g. `"Modal.traits.ModalRecordModal"`.

fields.name: name_override
fields.doc: `name: "InstanceName"` — instance-name override lowered to `name` on the trait reference. Disambiguates multiple rebinds of one source trait in a single orbital (the declaration identifier stays free for embed unification); absent, the declaration identifier is the name.

fields.name: events
fields.doc: Event-key renames in source order: `[("OPEN", "ADD_ITEM"), ...]`. Lowered to `events: { OPEN: "ADD_ITEM" }` on the trait reference.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Entity-field renames in source order: `[("title", "dishName"), ...]`. Lowered to `fields: { title: "dishName" }` on the trait reference. The inline phase rewrites `@entity.title` reads to `@entity.dishName`.

fields.name: config
fields.doc: Caller-supplied `config: { param: value, ... }` values at the trait-ref call site. Inline phase substitutes `@config.<param>` in the imported trait's effects/guards with these values. May carry full annotations (`@label`/`@description`/`@synonyms`/`@tier`) when the organism explicitly re-documents a knob. Lowered to `config: { ... }` on the trait reference.

fields.name: emits_scope
fields.doc: `emitsScope external|internal` override. Lowered to `emitsScope` on the trait reference.

name: State
doc: `state name [for duration] { transitions... }`.

fields.name: time_bound
fields.doc: Duration in milliseconds for `state name for 30s` form.

fields.name: transitions
fields.doc: All transitions out of this state, in source order.

fields.name: holds
fields.doc: `@holds <expr>`: a proposition over `@entity` that holds while the trait is in this state.

name: Transition
doc: `EVENT -> target [when (guard)] { effects... }`.

fields.name: ensures
fields.doc: `@ensures <expr>` lines: the outcome contract owed at this transition (`@fromEntity` is the row before it).

fields.name: guard_spans
fields.doc: L2 source-map spans captured while parsing `guard`, keyed by the JSON-pointer trail relative to the guard expression's own root (`""` for the guard's own span). Empty when there's no guard.

fields.name: effect_spans
fields.doc: Parallel to `effects`: `effect_spans[i]` holds the trail/span pairs captured while parsing `effects[i]`.

fields.name: term_match
fields.doc: `EVENT -> target match @entity.<f> { … }` sugar (Phase 2, pattern- matching doc §1(a)) — mutually exclusive with `guard`/`effects`, which stay `None`/empty when this is `Some` (`parser::trait_::parse_transition` enforces the exclusion; `when` + `match` together is a parse error). Pure L1 sugar: `lower::expand_term_match` turns each arm into one ordinary guarded `Transition` before anything downstream ever sees it.

name: TermMatch
doc: Transition-position term-level `match` (Phase 2). Dispatches on a VALUE (`@entity.<f>`/`@payload.<f>`, v1) rather than Phase 1's config-resolved TYPE — same `MatchPattern` arm vocabulary, reused as-is.

name: MatchScrutinee
doc: A term-match scrutinee: `@entity.<field>` / `@payload.<field>`, or the Phase-3a dotted destructuring form `@entity.<field>.<member>` / `@payload.<field>.<member>` where `<field>`'s declared type is a tagged struct union and `<member>` is its discriminating member (each variant's single-valued closed member, e.g. `type : "draw-shape"`). `@config.<knob>` (degenerate constant dispatch; use type-level `match` or a plain guard) and `@user.<field>` (fail-open class needs its own design pass) are parse errors, see `parser::trait_::parse_term_match_scrutinee`.

name: TermMatchArm
doc: One arm of a term-level `match`. `effects` mirrors `Transition::effects` (zero or more s-expressions, authoring order); `effect_spans` mirrors `Transition::effect_spans`.

name: Emit
doc: One entry in an `emits { }` block.  Two surface shapes (post-Phase 10): `EVENT [-> internal|external] [{ fields }]`  When `payload` is empty, the lower step resolves `event` against the orbital-scope `type EVENT = Event { ... }` alias registry and uses the alias's fields. Bare names with no matching alias produce a payloadless emit definition.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Semantic annotations (trailing `@description`/`@synonyms`/`@tier`), mirror of the entity-field + config-knob annotation layer. Feed the event matcher.

name: Listen
doc: One entry in a `listens { }` block.  Two shapes (post-Phase 10):  - **Cross-orbital**: `Source.EVENT -> TRIGGER [when (...)] [with { ... }]`. `event` is `"Source.EVENT"`, `triggers` names the local event to fire. Source and event are dot-separated.  - **Local (incoming trigger metadata)**: `EVENT [{ fields }]`. No source, no `->`. `event` is the bare key. When `payload` is empty, the lower step resolves against the orbital-scope alias registry (same rule as `Emit`).

fields.name: event
fields.doc: Source orbital and event in `Source.EVENT` form for the cross-orbital shape; bare key (`"REQUEST"`) for the local shape.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Inline payload field list for the local shape: `REQUEST { id : string!, foo : string }`. Empty for cross-orbital or payloadless locals.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Semantic annotations (trailing `@description`/`@synonyms`/`@tier`).

fields.name: target_trait
fields.doc: `-> Target.TRIGGER`: the imported trait that gains this route. Only an orbital import's `listens {}` carries one.

fields.name: external
fields.doc: `EVENT -> external { … }`: a declared external input, an event a client outside the program may send this trait.

fields.name: inbound
fields.doc: `EVENT -> inbound "name" answers ANSWER { … }`: the hook delivered to this event and the event that answers it.

name: InboundListen
doc: The `inbound "name" answers ANSWER` part of a local listen.

fields.name: verifies
fields.doc: `verifies "<header>" "<CREDENTIAL>"`: the kernel compares the header with the named credential.

name: InboundVerifies
doc: The `verifies "<header>" "<CREDENTIAL>"` part of an inbound listen.

name: Tick
doc: One entry in a `ticks { }` block.

fields.name: interval
fields.doc: Interval in milliseconds (or original cron string when not numeric).

fields.name: background
fields.doc: `[background]`: runs with no client mounted.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: `[visible]`: a browser tick that pauses while its trait's output is off screen.

fields.name: guard_spans
fields.doc: L2 source-map spans captured while parsing `guard`. See [`Transition::guard_spans`].

fields.name: effect_spans
fields.doc: Parallel to `effects`. See [`Transition::effect_spans`].

name: TickInterval
doc: How often a tick fires: a fixed interval or a cron expression.

fields.name: Millis
fields.doc: A fixed interval in milliseconds (`every 5s`).

fields.name: Cron
fields.doc: A quoted cron expression (`every "0 9 * * *"`).

name: ConfigField
doc: One entry in a `config { }` block.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Human-readable question prompt — `@label "..."` annotation on the line below the field declaration. Threads through to the .orb config block so the studio questionnaire can render it without inventing labels.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Long-form help text — `@description "..."` annotation on the line below the field declaration.

fields.name: synonyms
fields.doc: User-vocabulary synonyms — `@synonyms "..."` annotation on the line below the field declaration. Comma-separated free text that downstream consumers (the agent's catalog summary, the knob-embeddings bake) use to widen vocabulary recall for user prompts. e.g. `@synonyms "taller, shorter, pixel height"` on a `height` field lets the LLM connect "make it taller" to the `height` knob without inferring cold.

fields.name: tier
fields.doc: Decision-kind tier — `@tier "..."` annotation on the line below the field declaration. One of `domain`, `presentation`, `internal`. Drives the studio Questionnaire's filter + disclosure: `internal` knobs are hidden entirely, `presentation` knobs collapse under the "Polish wording" panel, `domain` knobs render inline. Untagged knobs are treated as `presentation` on the consumer side (safe default — most un-audited knobs are presentation polish). The L2 validator (`ORB_T_CONFIG_TIER_INVALID`) rejects any other value.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: `!` required marker — `fields : [FieldSpec]! = [...]`. Declares this knob must be supplied by every call site referencing the owning trait (the atom's own page binding is exempt). May coexist with a `default` (the default serves the demo page).

fields.name: event_refs
fields.doc: Dotted event atoms in `default`, keyed by their trail inside it — each must sit at an `event`-typed position.

name: EventField
doc: One field in an event payload schema.

name: Page
doc: `page /path [:: TypeAnnotation] -> Trait [, Trait...] [options]` or `page /path [:: TypeAnnotation] = Alias.pages.Upstream [-> Trait [, Trait...]]` (reference form).

fields.name: type_annotation
fields.doc: Optional `::` type annotation above the page declaration.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: When `Some`, this page is a reference to an imported page. The string is the dotted path (`Alias.pages.PageName`). When set, `traits` and `primary_entity` (if present) act as overrides on the imported page.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Explicit page name override from `page "/path" as PageName -> ...`. When `Some`, the lowerer uses it as the .orb `name` field verbatim; when `None`, a name is derived from the path. Explicit naming avoids fragile path-to-name heuristics — every committed .orb was authored with a hand-picked name that no single derivation rule reproduces.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: Nav icon name — `@icon "..."` annotation below the page line.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Human nav label — `@label "..."` annotation below the page line.

fields.name: roles
fields.doc: Nav entry roles — `@roles "a, b"` annotation below the page line.

fields.name: translation_of
fields.doc: `translationOf:` — the translation group this page belongs to.
